candidate_labels: Primary Colorectal Cancer with Ovarian Metastasis

Primary Peritoneal Carcinoma: Immunoprofile favoured ovarian origin rather than colonic, highly positive to CK7, negative to CK20
Genetic testing identified BRCA1 mutation (185delAG) at age 62
Histology of surgical specimens revealed peritoneal nodules of poorly differentiated papillary adenocarcinoma
Faint staining for ER, PR staining negative
Family history: breast cancer in mother and maternal grandmother at ages 34 and 41
Ovarian Cancer Metastasis to Colon: Poorly differentiated papillary adenocarcinoma of large bowel penetrated bowel wall and invaded adherent bladder
Mass contiguous with left lateral aspect of bladder, no associated pathological lymphadenopathy
Two separate peritoneal deposits, one within pelvis and one at terminal ileum
Laparotomy findings included bulky tumour adherent to left pelvic brim and pelvic side-wall
Associated extramural venous invasion, no metastatic lymph nodes (total of 3 found)
Primary Colorectal Cancer with Ovarian M: Biopsies confirmed very poorly differentiated papillary adenocarcinoma of sigmoid
Staging CT scan excluded macroscopic metastases, reported large bowel-related mass measuring 68 mm by 67 mm
Changes in bowel habits, faecal leakage, urgency, and left-sided abdominal discomfort at age 64
